subject: Finishes that connect living spaces
hook: Do my living-room units have to match my kitchen exactly?
fb:
"Does my living-room furniture have to match my kitchen?"

Not exactly. In fact, matching everything can make an open-plan space feel a bit flat. What works is one or two shared threads: the same handles, or the kitchen's accent colour picked up on a media wall or sideboard.

If you're stuck, bring a photo of your kitchen to a free design consultation and we'll put samples side by side. Got a question about your own rooms? Ask away below.

gbp:
"Do my living-room units have to match my kitchen exactly?"

Not exactly, but they should clearly belong together. In open-plan homes, furniture that copies the kitchen finish everywhere can feel flat, while units with nothing in common look like they came from different houses.

We usually recommend keeping one or two shared elements: the same handles across both areas, or the kitchen's accent finish repeated on a sideboard, alcove unit or media wall. Finishes available include oak-effect, charcoal, black woodgrain, matt white and matt black.

At a free, no-obligation design consultation we put samples next to your existing kitchen and flooring so you can see the combination before anything is made. Everything is then built to measure in our Hanley workshop and fitted by our own team.

Learn more about the furniture we make.
